countingMethod: A checked unit is one related factual lesson group, one full question (prompt, all options, explanations and worked example), one glossary definition with all aliases, or one analogy mapping/limit. Counts do not pretend each sentence or assertion is an independent claim.

esb-what-embedded: Embedded software serves a device purpose; input, decisions, functions and state remain software concepts.
Firmware describes stored device software and need not be unchangeable; supported programming enables updates.
Microcontroller focus and separation of host logic tests from board choice.
Illustrative below/above/invalid data cases give normal/alert/fault; example choices are not universal sensor rules.
Bare metal excludes an operating system, including an RTOS, while retaining startup/library support.
Embedded systems may use an operating system.
Available memory and permitted signals are hardware constraints.
Real-time correctness can depend on arrival time rather than maximum speed.
Promptly returning operations and defined fault outcomes are explicit course project requirements.
esb-mcu-memory-peripherals: MCUs combine core(s), memory and interfaces; surrounding boards can add memory, power and connections.
CPU executes instructions; working RAM holds variables and buffers.
Ordinary SRAM is volatile; firmware retention does not imply measurement retention.
Flash supports nonvolatile program/data storage, internal or external depending on chip.
RP2040 has on-chip SRAM and an external flash interface; board flash is distinct from chip memory.
CPU, firmware storage, RAM and peripheral roles in the toy application are separated.
Peripheral hardware can perform configured work between foreground instructions.
Memory maps distinguish address ranges; access behavior is not uniform.
Peripheral registers control or observe hardware including pin configuration/input; accesses may have side effects.
Persistent settings require a supported store/load design rather than ordinary RAM alone.
esb-datasheet-and-board: Component datasheets describe functions, limits, registers and conditions.
Board manuals/schematics describe actual component connections.
SDKs supply supported libraries, headers, examples and build configuration.
Chip pin functions, board allocation and SDK names/configuration are separate.
Exact board model/revision and controlling component must be identified.
Official Pico/Pico W blink branches use differing LED control paths.
Successful compilation does not establish selected board or loaded image correctness.
Documented onboard indication is a bounded first observation without external signal wiring.
External inputs require exact electrical-limit, ground-reference and power checks.
Unknown voltages/high-current loads must not be connected directly to MCU pins; course examples require no such wiring.
esb-build-flash-run: Host source editing alone does not program a target.
Cross compiler runs on a host and targets a specified processor/environment.
Preprocessing precedes compilation proper and handles inclusion.
Compilation/assembly produce translated objects; linking combines parts, resolves references and lays out an image.
Declaration can permit compilation despite missing implementation, with later linking failure.
Successful build does not prove image transfer or correct runtime behavior.
Supported image format and programming route are target-specific.
Original Pico documented BOOTSEL startup exposes USB mass-storage programming.
Supported UF2 transfer is interpreted by boot software and followed by restart; not every MCU supports UF2.
Observe specified behavior and match board/build before interpreting transfer success as functional correctness.
esb-reset-startup: Reset restarts execution; flash programming changes storage and tools may combine them.
Application first visible output follows supporting startup work.
CMSIS Cortex-M template has reset handler, initial stack pointer and exception/interrupt vectors.
Template reset handler typically calls SystemInit, then C runtime initialization and main.
This is a scoped software model; device/toolchain/project determine startup.
Static-duration C variables have whole-program lifetime and are initialized before program startup.
C11 freestanding application entry name/type are implementation-defined; main is not universally the first reset instruction.
C runtime initialization is distinct from hardware RAM clearing/retention.
Bootloaders load/start another image and can offer programming or recovery; capabilities vary.
Some devices start from manufacturer ROM; RP2040 boot ROM participates in startup and USB boot.
Transfer/debug/startup/hardware-init milestones separate earlier failures from later decision logic.
Some resets preserve RAM or retention storage; supported runtime may reinitialize application data.
esb-loop-state: Cooperative foreground jobs return control to permit later jobs; interrupts/other cores are separate.
Repeated execution needs explicit remembered state.
Accepted press event differs from physical held level; input is assumed debounced.
Published pseudocode consumes at most one press event per loop pass.
Only PRESS toggles OFF/ON; no event preserves state.
The four-pass trace is OFF, ON, ON, OFF.
Using a held level repeatedly would toggle on every pass.
Host event/state checks do not validate button wiring, voltage or board timing.
An indefinite earlier wait prevents later statements in that foreground execution.
Bounded work and explicit progress support responsiveness; loop structure/interrupts/RTOS alone prove no deadline.

corrections: Removed interrupt handler/interrupt handlers aliases from Interrupt: those name the service routine, not the request. Existing embedded-isr now owns the intended routine meaning.
Separated state transition/state transitions from State machine into a precise new entry, including the possibility of a self-transition.

Corrected contextual glossary sense selection: volatile working RAM now resolves to volatile memory; register side effects have a hardware-specific entry; ordinary input limits, output/access path and happens-before phrases were rewritten to avoid unrelated algorithm, OS, database or synchronization entries.

Replaced insufficiently targeted source attribution: the real-time glossary/question cite RTEMS deadline material, board-wiring question cites board documentation/schematics, safe debug connections cite the vendor ground-reference precautions, and Bare metal cites the manufacturer's explicit OS/RTOS exclusion.
clarifications: Bare-metal wording was already OS-free. Added an explicit RTOS exclusion to both lesson and glossary so beginners cannot mistake a small operating system for bare metal.

Added scoped C static-duration lifetime and initialization facts, linked to N1570 5.1.2, 5.1.2.1 and corroborated by 6.2.4 paragraph 3; retained the distinction between runtime initialization and physical reset retention.
gaps: No physical board, electrical behavior, flash operation or worst-case timing was tested; the module claims only source-checked device examples and host decision-model checks.
Compiler installation and commands remain board-specific; the original Pico BOOTSEL/UF2 route is a documented illustration, not a universal flashing procedure.

Executable C teaching belongs to module 2; foundations deliberately uses one labeled pseudocode loop. Production bootloaders, linker scripts and retention implementation are outside the agreed introductory scope.
sourcePassages: RP2040 datasheet sections 1.2–1.4 (chip/core/pins), 2.2 (address map), 2.3–2.4 (interrupt/debug), 2.6 (ROM/SRAM/external flash), 2.7–2.8 (boot/reset/USB), 4.2 (UART FIFO read effects), and XIP FLUSH register retention.

CMSIS startup description and template: initial MSP, reset handler, vectors, SystemInit, __PROGRAM_START and runtime/main; SystemInit note distinguishes runtime .bss initialization from earlier hardware configuration.

Official Pico documentation source: board overview/resources and schematic links; SDK board selection; first binary BOOTSEL/UF2/reboot flow; debug-probe reference/ground warning. Official blink source distinguishes PICO_DEFAULT_LED_PIN and CYW43_WL_GPIO_LED_PIN.

GCC Overall Options stage ordering and -c; Preprocessor Options preprocessing before compilation; Installation Configuration host/build/target definitions. GNU ld Scripts documents output section mapping and memory layout. STM32G030 datasheet memory description corroborates internal flash as an alternative to the RP2040 external-flash example.
Official C11 draft N1570 local original PDF and extracted text: 5.1.2 paragraph 1; 5.1.2.1 paragraph 1; 6.2.4 paragraph 3; 6.7.9 paragraph 10.
QP/C conceptual model non-preemptive loop and task-level response; SRS state transition and event processing descriptions. No QP-specific scheduling guarantee is attributed to the toy superloop.
RTEMS Overview 2.2 real-time application systems and glossary deadline; Altera Bare-Metal Developer Center expressly excludes OS/RTOS; USB-IF About expands Universal Serial Bus.

NIST firmware definitions corroborate role/storage terminology; the official replaceable Pico firmware image workflow supports updateability without treating traditional ROM-only definitions as universal.

checks.questions: All 18 prompts, 72 options and explanations, answer keys and worked examples read and independently assessed; no answer-key changes required. Required evidence stays visible with every analogy closed.
checks.glossary: All original 53 definitions/aliases plus two added entries reviewed. glossary-links inspected; conceptual mismatches corrected locally. Four coverage candidates are state/event labels OFF/PRESS and editorial How it maps/Where it stops.
checks.links: 15 unique active lesson/question URLs checked over network, 0 failing; each attached source inspected for supporting content.
checks.hardware: No physical validation performed or claimed.

esb-what-embedded.rationale: Added receptionist procedure maps input, explicit decision and output, including invalid input. Its limit explicitly forbids human judgment substituting for specified timing/failure rules; all tested facts remain visible.

esb-mcu-memory-peripherals.rationale: Added workshop separates CPU execution, retained instructions, working RAM and peripheral roles. Its limit explicitly permits RAM execution and register side effects; it does not claim all memory behaves like storage.

esb-datasheet-and-board.rationale: Added appliance specification/room wiring/control interface maps chip datasheet, board schematic and SDK. Its stated limit preserves wiring and electrical limits independently of software convenience.

esb-build-flash-run.rationale: Added preparing, assembling and delivering an instruction pack separates compile, link and transfer. The limit keeps target compatibility and functional observation necessary; it does not imply transfer proves behavior.

esb-reset-startup.rationale: Added shop-opening preparation maps reset/startup milestones to prerequisites for application execution. Device-dependent order and RAM retention are explicit limits; C initialization and required facts remain outside.

esb-loop-state.rationale: Added service-desk round maps one foreground execution visiting short jobs and retaining state. It explicitly excludes a proof about interrupts, other cores, shared-data safety or response deadlines.
